name: Mastodon 1/2 in. 12-Strand Rigging Rope
title: Mastodon 1/2 in. Rigging Rope: 12-Strand Lowering Line
meta: Mastodon rigging rope in 1/2 in. 12-strand braid for lowering small to mid-size wood. How to use it, splice it, inspect it and when to retire it.
tagline: A 1/2 in. 12-strand rigging line for everyday limb lowering and light removals.
summary: Mastodon rigging rope is a 1/2 in. 12-strand braided line built for lowering limbs and small wood rather than for climbing. The single-braid construction is easy to inspect and quick to splice, which makes it a practical choice for a crew's everyday lowering line.
highlights: 1/2 in. diameter for small to mid-size rigging
12-strand single braid, easy to splice and inspect
Handles well through blocks and porta-wraps
Rigging only, not for life support
Good spare or second line on the truck

body.h: Where a 1/2 in. rigging line fits
p: Half-inch line covers most of the pieces a typical residential crew lowers: limbs off a spar, tops on small trees, brush bundles over a roof or fence. It runs smoothly through a mid-size block and around a porta-wrap, and it is light enough that a groundie can flake it out and pull it back without a fight.

Twelve-strand braid has no separate cover, so every strand is visible. Cuts, fused spots and pulled strands are easy to find, and the rope splices with a simple bury, so you can put an eye in the end for a running bowline alternative or a sling.

Rigging line takes shock loads, and a piece that free-falls before the rope catches it can load the system far beyond the weight of the wood. Size the line, block and anchor for the piece, keep drops short, and let the groundie run friction instead of locking off. Check the manufacturer's rated strength and working load before you plan a big pick.

Wash grit out with plain water, dry it out of the sun and store it in a bag. Retire it when strands are cut, glazed or stiff. Do not climb on rigging rope. See our climbing rope range for life-support line.

faq.q: Can I climb on Mastodon rigging rope?
faq.a: No. It is a rigging line. Climb only on rope sold and rated for life support and used per ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Why choose a 12-strand rigging line?
faq.a: It is easy to inspect, easy to splice and handles well through blocks, which suits everyday lowering.

name: Yale XTC 16-Strand White Climbing Rope
title: Yale XTC 16-Strand Climbing Rope (White): Buyer's Guide
meta: Yale XTC climbing rope in white: a classic 1/2 in. 16-strand line that grips hitches well and wears hard. What it suits, care tips and how to inspect it.
tagline: A classic 1/2 in. 16-strand line for traditional hitch climbing and everyday work.
summary: Yale XTC climbing rope is a 1/2 in. 16-strand line that has been a standard on tree crews for years. The white version is plain and easy to inspect, and the firm braid holds traditional friction hitches well.
highlights: Firm hand that holds friction hitches
Plain white makes dirt and damage easy to see

p: Sixteen-strand climbing line has a braided cover over a core, a slightly larger diameter than modern 24-strand lines and a firm feel. That firmness is why many climbers still like it for doubled-rope work with a Blake's hitch or a Distel: the hitch grabs predictably and releases without drama.

The white colorway is about as plain as rope gets. It shows dirt, sap and pulled strands right away, which helps when you inspect before each climb, and it is easy to tell apart from a crew's colored rigging lines. Pair it with a hitch cord sized for half-inch line.

XTC works for both moving rope and stationary rope systems, though some mechanical devices are built around 11 to 12 mm line, so check the device maker's approved rope list first. Expect it to stiffen a little with use and grime.

Climbing line is life-support equipment. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every climb, retire it when the cover is cut or glazed or the core feels damaged, and get proper training before you trust it. Browse the rest of our 16-strand climbing rope options to compare colors and lengths.

faq.q: What diameter is Yale XTC?
faq.a: It is a 1/2 in. 16-strand climbing line.

faq.q: Does XTC work with mechanical devices?
faq.a: Some devices accept 1/2 in. line and some do not. Check the device manufacturer's approved rope list before you pair them.

highlights: 200 ft for tall trees and long redirects
Size that suits most hitches and many SRS devices
Bright pattern is easy to see in the canopy

p: An 11.7mm line sits in the middle of the arborist range. It is thick enough to hold a Distel or VT on a matching hitch cord and to run through the many SRS devices built around 11 to 13 mm rope, yet light enough to carry up a big tree.

Two hundred feet matters when you are tied in high and working doubled, because a doubled system needs twice the height to reach the ground. It also gives you spare tail for redirects on wide-spreading crowns, and a long line can later be cut down into a shorter climbing line and a lanyard.

Match hitch cord to the rope diameter and test the hitch low before you commit to it. If you run a mechanical device, confirm the rope is on its approved list. Keep the line in a bag, away from saw fuel and the bed of the truck.

Climbing line is life-support equipment. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every climb, retire it when the cover is cut or glazed or the core feels damaged, and get proper training before you trust it. faq.q: Will Sawtooth work with SRS devices?
faq.a: Many SRS devices accept 11.7mm rope, but always check the device maker's approved rope list.

title: Marlow Maverick 11.5mm Climbing Rope: Buyer's Guide
meta: Marlow Maverick climbing rope at 11.5mm: a compact arborist line for hitch and device climbing. What it suits, how to pair it, and how to inspect and retire it.

summary: The Marlow Maverick climbing rope is an 11.5mm arborist line that sits at the slimmer end of the typical range. It suits climbers who want a lighter line for long days while still running the hitches and devices most crews already use.

Works with many hitches and mechanical devices
Made by Marlow, a long-time UK rope maker

p: At 11.5mm the Maverick is slightly thinner than the 11.7 to 11.8mm lines many climbers know. That saves a little weight in the bag and on your saddle, and a slimmer rope feeds a bit more freely through a hitch or device. The trade-off is that you may need a thinner hitch cord, or a few more wraps, for the same grab.
Marlow builds its arborist ropes for both moving rope and stationary rope work. Use it doubled with a friction hitch, or as a single line on a device that lists 11.5mm rope as compatible.

Test any new rope and hitch pairing near the ground first. Check the hitch cord diameter, the device's rope range and how the system behaves when the rope is wet or dirty, since all of these change friction.

Climbing line is life-support equipment. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every climb, retire it when the cover is cut or glazed or the core feels damaged, and get proper training before you trust it. name: Marlow Vega 11.7mm Climbing Rope, Lime/Gray
title: Marlow Vega 11.7mm Climbing Rope (Lime/Gray)
meta: Marlow Vega climbing rope in 11.7mm lime and gray: a low-stretch arborist line for SRS and hitch climbing. How it handles, setup tips and inspection basics.
tagline: A low-stretch 11.7mm Marlow line in lime and gray for SRS and doubled-rope work.
summary: Marlow Vega climbing rope is an 11.7mm arborist line known for low stretch and a firm, round braid. The lime and gray colorway stands out against bark and foliage, and the line suits both single rope and doubled-rope climbing.
highlights: 11.7mm diameter, the middle of the arborist range
Low stretch for efficient SRS ascents
Firm round braid that runs well in devices

p: Low stretch is the main draw. When you ascend a single rope, every bit of stretch is effort you lose, and a static-feeling line like Vega puts more of each foot push into height. It also gives a direct, predictable feel when you descend on a mechanical device.

At 11.7mm it fits the rope range of most popular SRS devices and holds a well-matched friction hitch for moving rope work. The lime and gray pattern is easy to spot in the canopy and easy to tell apart from rigging lines on the ground.

Because it stretches little, Vega transmits shock more directly, so avoid slack in your system and never use it for rigging. Check the device maker's approved rope list and test any hitch pairing low before you climb.

Climbing line is life-support equipment. Use it only within the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, inspect it before every climb, retire it when the cover is cut or glazed or the core feels damaged, and get proper training before you trust it. See more 24-strand climbing rope to compare.

faq.q: Is Marlow Vega good for SRS?
faq.a: Yes. Its low stretch and 11.7mm diameter suit most SRS devices, but confirm your device's approved rope list.

faq.q: Can I use Vega for doubled-rope climbing?
faq.a: Yes, with a hitch cord matched to the diameter, tested near the ground first.

name: Pensafe Tool Tether Carabiner
title: Pensafe Tool Tether Carabiner for Dropped-Object Safety
meta: Pensafe tool tether carabiner for clipping hand saws, wrenches and small tools to your saddle or bucket. What it is for, how to use it and what not to clip.
tagline: A tool-tethering carabiner for keeping small tools attached when you work at height.
summary: The Pensafe tool tether carabiner is made for clipping tool lanyards and small gear to your saddle, belt or bucket so nothing falls on the crew below. It is an accessory carabiner for tool control, not life support.
highlights: For tool tethering and dropped-object prevention
Clips tool lanyards to saddles, belts and buckets
Not rated for life support or rigging

p: A dropped wrench or hand saw from 40 feet can seriously hurt a groundie or punch through a roof. Tethering tools is a simple way to cut that risk, especially in bucket work over traffic or near houses, where the drop zone is hard to keep clear.

A tool tether carabiner gives you a dedicated, quick clip point for tool lanyards. Clip it to a gear loop or bucket rail, then clip the tool's lanyard to it. Keep tool tethers on their own clip points so they never get mixed up with your climbing system.

This is an accessory carabiner. Never use it in your climbing system, as a lanyard connector, or for rigging. Life-support connectors must be rated and used per ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions. Check the tool weight limit on the tether and lanyard you pair it with.
Inspect the gate and body for bends, sharp edges and grit, and replace it if the gate sticks. For rated connectors, see our carabiners and hardware range.

faq.q: Can I use the Pensafe tool tether carabiner for climbing?
faq.a: No. It is for tool tethering only. Use rated, life-support connectors in your climbing system.

faq.q: What tools can I tether with it?
faq.a: Small hand tools such as wrenches and hand saws, within the weight limit of the tether system you use.

name: 1/2 in. Whoopie Sling with Medium Ring
title: 1/2 in. Whoopie Sling with Medium Ring for Rigging
h1: 1/2 in. Whoopie Sling with Medium Ring
meta: A 1/2 in. whoopie sling with a medium ring for setting rigging blocks and redirects. How the adjustable sling works, how to set it and how to inspect it.
tagline: An adjustable 1/2 in. sling with a ring for quick block and redirect anchors.
summary: A whoopie sling is an adjustable sling spliced from hollow-braid line, and this 1/2 in. version comes with a medium ring on the fixed eye. It lets you set a rigging block or redirect on stems of many sizes and tighten it snug without tying knots.
highlights: Medium ring on the fixed eye
Fits a wide range of stem sizes
Easy to untie after a heavy load

p: A whoopie is a length of hollow-braid line spliced so that one part of the rope runs inside itself. Pull the tail and the loop shrinks; load it and the outer braid grips the inner, locking the length. That lets one sling fit a spar, a fork or a big leader without a girth hitch that is too long or too short.

The ring on the fixed eye gives you a clean attachment point for a block or a redirect, and it helps the sling choke down evenly on the stem. Many climbers use a whoopie and ring as a quick anchor for a lowering block on medium-size removals.

Snug the sling tight before loading so it cannot slip down the stem, and keep the adjustable section within the length the maker allows. Check the rated strength of the sling and the ring, and stay well inside it, because rigging loads spike when wood drops before the line catches it.
Inspect for cut or fused fibers, pulled strands and damage at the splices. Retire it if in doubt. More options are in our adjustable slings range.

faq.q: What is a whoopie sling used for?
faq.a: Setting rigging blocks, redirects and anchors on stems of different sizes, without knots.

faq.q: Can I use a whoopie sling as a climbing anchor?
faq.a: Only if the specific sling is rated and approved for life support. Most rigging whoopies are for rigging only.

name: Haix Protector Prime Chainsaw Boots, Orange
title: Haix Protector Prime Chainsaw Boots (Orange)
h1: Haix Protector Prime Chainsaw Boots, Orange
meta: Haix Protector Prime chainsaw boots in orange: cut-protective leather boots for ground saw work and climbing. Fit, features, care and what the rating means.
tagline: Cut-protective leather chainsaw boots with high-visibility orange for saw-heavy work.
summary: The Haix Protector Prime is a leather chainsaw boot with cut-protective inserts, made for arborists and forestry workers who run a saw on the ground and in the tree. The orange upper adds visibility on the job.
highlights: Lug sole for grip on slopes and brush
Suited to spurs and long days on foot

p: Feet are one of the parts of the body most often hit by a saw, especially when bucking on the ground or limbing a felled tree. Chainsaw boots carry protective layers designed to slow and clog a moving chain, giving you a better chance than a plain work boot. Check the boot's label for its cut-protection standard and class.
The Protector Prime pairs that protection with a supportive upper and a lugged sole that holds in mud, leaves and on slopes. The high, stiff ankle also works well with climbing spurs on removals.
Try boots on with the socks you work in and allow some break-in time. A good fit matters on long days hauling brush and running a chipper.

Clean off mud and sap, let them dry naturally away from heaters, and treat the leather regularly. Retire boots that take a chain cut, because protective fibers do not recover. Chainsaw boots supplement, never replace, chaps and safe saw handling. Compare more arborist boots.

faq.q: Are Haix Protector Prime boots chainsaw protective?
faq.a: Yes. They are chainsaw boots with cut-protective inserts. Check the label for the exact standard and class.

faq.q: Can I wear them with climbing spurs?
faq.a: Many climbers do, as the stiff upper and ankle support suit spur work. Check spur fit with your boot size.

name: CAMP Oval XL 3Lock Carabiner
title: CAMP Oval XL 3Lock Carabiner: Triple-Lock Oval
meta: CAMP Oval XL 3Lock: a large aluminum oval carabiner with a triple-action auto-locking gate, made for pulleys, hitch systems and gear-heavy arborist setups.
tagline: A large aluminum oval with a triple-action auto-lock gate for pulleys and devices.
summary: The CAMP Oval XL 3Lock carabiner is a large aluminum oval with a triple-action auto-locking gate. Its symmetrical shape keeps pulleys, rope wrenches and hitch systems sitting square, and the bigger size makes room for several items.

p: An oval's symmetrical shape lets a pulley or device sit in the middle of the basket instead of sliding to one side. That keeps loading even and stops pulleys from twisting, which is why ovals are a common choice for hitch climbing systems, micro pulleys and rope-wrench setups.

The XL size gives extra room for a pulley plus a hitch tender or a second connector, and it is easier to handle with gloves. The triple-action gate needs a twist and push to open, so it resists accidental opening against bark and rope.
Ovals are generally rated lower than D shapes because the load sits further from the spine, so check the strength markings on the carabiner and make sure it suits your system.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. Compare more auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: What is the CAMP Oval XL 3Lock good for?
faq.a: Holding pulleys, hitch systems and devices centered, with room for multiple items.

faq.q: Is a triple-lock gate required for climbing?
faq.a: Follow ANSI Z133, your employer's rules and the device maker's instructions. Many arborists prefer triple-action gates for life support.

name: DMM Ultra O Locksafe Carabiner with Captive Bar
title: DMM Ultra O Locksafe Carabiner with Captive Bar
h1: DMM Ultra O Locksafe Carabiner with Captive Bar
meta: DMM Ultra O Locksafe carabiner with captive bar: an aluminum oval with an auto-locking gate and a bar that holds a device or pulley in place on the spine.
tagline: An aluminum oval with a Locksafe gate and a captive bar to keep devices in place.
summary: The DMM Ultra O Locksafe carabiner with captive bar is a large aluminum oval with DMM's auto-locking Locksafe gate. The captive bar holds a pulley, device or sling in position so it cannot rotate or slide into a poor loading position.
highlights: Captive bar holds items in position
Good for pulleys and friction devices

p: A captive bar closes off part of the carabiner so whatever is clipped there stays put. With a pulley or a friction device, that means the item cannot roll around to the gate side or cross-load when you shift your weight, a common problem on hitch systems with lots of movement.

The Ultra O's oval shape keeps a pulley centered, and the Locksafe gate locks itself when it closes. Many climbers build a dedicated hitch system around a captive-bar oval so the setup stays the same climb after climb.
Check that the device or pulley fits the captive section correctly and that nothing loads the bar or gate. Read the strength markings and DMM's instructions for the captive-bar version.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. Browse our auto-locking carabiners for more.

faq.q: Why use a captive-bar carabiner?
faq.a: It keeps a pulley or device in the right position so it cannot rotate onto the gate or cross-load.

faq.q: Can I remove the captive bar?
faq.a: Follow DMM's instructions for the specific model. Do not modify life-support connectors.

name: ISC Aluminum HMS Carabiner
title: ISC Aluminum HMS Carabiner: Auto-Locking Pear Shape
meta: ISC aluminum HMS carabiner: a pear-shaped auto-locking connector with a wide gate and roomy basket for hitches, lanyards and anchor work in tree climbing.
tagline: A wide pear-shaped aluminum connector for hitches, anchors and lanyards.
summary: The ISC aluminum HMS carabiner is a pear-shaped auto-locking connector with a wide end that suits hitches, rope and multiple attachments. It is a versatile all-round carabiner for a climbing kit.
highlights: HMS (pear) shape with a wide basket
Room for rope and multiple items

p: HMS carabiners have a wide end that gives rope and hitches room to sit and turn. That makes them handy for tying in a friction hitch, connecting a lanyard, or building an anchor with more than one item in the basket.

The aluminum body keeps weight low on a crowded saddle, and the wide gate opening is easy to clip with gloves. Many climbers keep a couple of HMS carabiners for general connections and use ovals for pulleys.
Keep loads along the spine and avoid letting items rest across the gate. Check the strength markings and that the gate type meets your system's requirements.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. See more auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: What does HMS mean on a carabiner?
faq.a: It refers to the pear shape originally designed for the Munter hitch, with a wide end for rope.

faq.q: Is aluminum strong enough for tree climbing?
faq.a: Yes, if the carabiner is rated for life support and inspected. Aluminum shows wear faster than steel, so check it often.

name: ISC Aluminum Oval Triple-Locking Carabiner
title: ISC Oval Carabiner: Aluminum Triple-Locking Gate
meta: ISC aluminum oval carabiner with a triple-locking gate: a symmetrical connector that keeps pulleys and devices centered in hitch climbing and rigging setups.
tagline: A symmetrical aluminum oval with a triple-action gate for pulleys and devices.
summary: The ISC oval carabiner is an aluminum connector with a triple-locking gate and a symmetrical shape. It keeps pulleys, swivels and devices sitting in the center of the basket, which is why ovals are a staple of hitch climbing systems.

body.h: Where an oval earns its spot
p: Clip a micro pulley onto a D-shaped carabiner and it slides toward the narrow end, twisting the pulley. On an oval it sits square, and the load stays even. That simple trait makes ovals the go-to connector for hitch tending pulleys, rope wrench tethers and swivel setups.
The triple-action gate requires two moves before it opens, which keeps it closed when it rubs against rope, bark or other gear. ISC's aluminum version keeps weight down on a full saddle.
Ovals usually carry a lower rating than D shapes, so check the markings and make sure it suits the job. Avoid cross-loading and loading over edges.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. Compare other auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: Why are oval carabiners used with pulleys?
faq.a: Their symmetrical shape keeps a pulley centered so it does not twist under load.

faq.q: Does a triple-locking gate open with one hand?
faq.a: Yes, with practice, but it takes deliberate twist-and-push movements, which is the point.

name: ISC Compact Oval Supersafe Carabiner
title: ISC Compact Oval Supersafe Carabiner
meta: ISC compact oval carabiner with a Supersafe auto-locking gate: a small, symmetrical connector for micro pulleys and tight hitch systems in tree climbing.
tagline: A compact oval with ISC's Supersafe auto-locking gate for tight hitch systems.
summary: The ISC compact oval carabiner with a Supersafe gate is a small, symmetrical connector for micro pulleys and compact hitch systems. Its auto-locking gate is designed to resist accidental opening against rope and bark.

p: A smaller oval keeps a hitch system short, which means the hitch sits closer to your bridge and you lose less height when tending slack. It also cuts bulk and weight on a saddle already loaded with lanyards, saws and slings.

The oval shape keeps a micro pulley or swivel centered so it runs true. The Supersafe gate is ISC's auto-locking design; take time to practice opening it with gloves so you can work it smoothly in the tree.
Check that your pulley and hitch cord eyes fit inside the compact basket without crowding the gate. Read the strength markings and ISC's instructions before use.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. See more auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: What is a compact oval carabiner used for?
faq.a: Micro pulleys and short hitch systems where a full-size oval adds bulk.

faq.q: Is the Supersafe gate auto-locking?
faq.a: Yes. Check ISC's instructions for how the specific gate operates.

name: Pro-Climb Double-Locking Aluminum Carabiner
title: Pro-Climb Double-Locking Aluminum Carabiner
meta: Pro-Climb double-locking aluminum carabiner: an affordable auto-locking connector for lanyards, hitch systems and general tree climbing connections.
tagline: An affordable aluminum auto-locking carabiner for everyday climbing connections.
summary: The Pro-Climb double-locking carabiner is an aluminum connector with a two-action auto-locking gate. It is a practical, affordable choice for lanyards, hitch systems and the everyday connections in a climbing kit.
highlights: Good value for stocking a kit

p: Every climber goes through carabiners: connecting a flipline, hanging a saw, building a hitch system. A double-locking aluminum carabiner covers most of those jobs at a fair price, which makes it easy to keep spares in the truck and to outfit new climbers.

The two-action gate locks automatically when it closes and opens with a twist then a pull. It is quicker than a triple-action gate, so check that a double-action gate is acceptable for your use under your company's rules and ANSI Z133.
Read the strength markings and keep loads along the spine. Aluminum wears faster than steel where rope runs over it, so look for grooves and sharp edges.

Carabiners in a climbing system are life-support gear. Use only connectors rated for the purpose, follow ANSI Z133 and the maker's instructions, load them along the major axis, and inspect the gate, spring and body before each use. Compare our auto-locking carabiners.

faq.q: What does double-locking mean?
faq.a: The gate needs two actions, typically a twist and then a pull, to open, and it locks itself when it closes.

faq.q: Is a double-locking gate OK for climbing?
faq.a: Check ANSI Z133, your employer's rules and the maker's instructions. Some setups call for triple-action gates.

name: Husqvarna 520iLX Battery String Trimmer (Tool Only)
title: Husqvarna 520iLX Battery Trimmer, Straight Shaft
meta: Husqvarna 520iLX battery string trimmer with a straight shaft, sold as a bare tool. Uses Husqvarna's 36V (40V max) battery platform. Fit, use and care tips.
tagline: A pro-grade straight-shaft battery trimmer for cleanup on tree and landscape jobs.
summary: The Husqvarna 520iLX is a straight-shaft battery string trimmer from Husqvarna's professional range, sold here as a bare tool. It runs on the same battery platform as Husqvarna's battery saws and blowers, so crews can share packs across tools.
highlights: Straight shaft for reach under shrubs and along fences
Quiet enough for residential and early starts
No mixing fuel or pull starting
specs: Tool only, battery and charger separate

body.h: Why a battery trimmer on a tree crew
p: Trimmers do a lot of small jobs around tree work: clearing around a stump before grinding, knocking back brush to get the chipper in, and cleaning up edges at the end of a job. A battery trimmer handles that without hauling mixed fuel, and it starts with a trigger rather than a cord.
Lower noise also helps when you start early in a neighborhood or work near customers. The straight shaft gives better reach under hedges and along fence lines than a curved shaft.

This listing is the bare tool, so you need a compatible Husqvarna battery and charger. If your crew already runs Husqvarna battery saws or blowers, you can share packs. Check runtime against the battery you pair it with.

Wear eye and hearing protection, keep bystanders clear of flying debris, and inspect the guard and head before use. Clean grass and sap off the head and vents after each day. See more battery-powered equipment.

faq.q: Does the 520iLX come with a battery?
faq.a: No. This is the bare tool. Batteries and charger are sold separately.

faq.q: Is it 36V or 40V?
faq.a: Husqvarna's platform is 36V nominal, often marketed as 40V max in the US. They are the same batteries.

name: Husqvarna K1 PACE Battery Power Cutter
title: Husqvarna K1 PACE Battery Power Cutter: Buyer's Guide
h1: Husqvarna K1 PACE Battery Power Cutter
meta: Husqvarna K1 PACE battery power cutter for cutting concrete, pavers and pipe without fuel or exhaust. What it does, where it fits and the safety basics.
tagline: A battery cut-off saw for concrete, pavers and pipe on hardscape-heavy jobs.
summary: The Husqvarna K1 PACE is a battery-powered power cutter for concrete, stone, pavers and pipe. It runs on Husqvarna's PACE battery system, so there is no mixed fuel or exhaust, which helps for indoor or tight-quarters cutting.
highlights: Battery power cutter, no fuel or exhaust
Runs on Husqvarna's PACE battery system
Cuts concrete, pavers, stone and pipe with the right blade

body.h: Where it fits for tree and landscape crews
p: Tree work regularly meets hardscape: a curb or paver edge in the way of a stump grinder, a root growing under a slab, irrigation pipe that needs cutting during planting or root work. A power cutter makes those cuts quickly, and the K1 PACE does it without fuel, exhaust or a pull cord.

That matters in garages, courtyards and close to buildings, where a gas cut-off saw is noisy and fumy. It is mainly a hardscape and utility tool rather than a tree tool, so it suits crews that also do landscape or site work.

Use only blades rated for the material and the saw's speed. Cut wet where possible to control silica dust, and follow silica rules for your area. Wear eye, hearing and respiratory protection and stay clear of the kickback zone. Get trained before use.
Batteries and chargers are part of the PACE system, so check what is included with your kit. Keep the saw clean and dry. More tools are in our battery-powered equipment range.

faq.q: What can the Husqvarna K1 PACE cut?
faq.a: Concrete, stone, pavers, masonry and pipe, with a blade rated for the material.

faq.q: Does it use the same battery as Husqvarna's 36V tools?
faq.a: No. It uses Husqvarna's PACE battery system.

name: Husqvarna T542iXP Battery Top-Handle Chainsaw (Tool Only)
title: Husqvarna T542iXP Battery Top-Handle Chainsaw
meta: Husqvarna T542iXP battery top-handle chainsaw, tool only: a pro climbing saw for in-tree pruning and removals. Bar options, batteries, safety and care tips.
tagline: A pro battery top-handle saw for in-tree pruning and light removals.
summary: The Husqvarna T542iXP is a battery-powered top-handle chainsaw built for arborists working in the tree. Sold as a tool only, it runs on Husqvarna's 36V platform and gives climbers a quiet, instant-start saw with no fuel to carry.
highlights: Instant trigger start, no pull cord
specs: Tool only, battery and charger separate

p: A battery top-handle removes two daily annoyances in the tree: pull-starting a saw on a lanyard and breathing exhaust while you prune. The T542iXP starts with the trigger and stops when you let go, which also makes it quieter and easier to communicate with the ground crew.
It is a working saw for pruning, crown reduction and piecing out smaller wood on removals. Many climbers carry a spare battery on the saddle or send one up on a tag line.

Top-handle saws are designed for trained arborists working in trees. Use a two-handed grip whenever possible, tether the saw with a chainsaw lanyard, and follow ANSI Z133 and Husqvarna's instructions. Never treat the quiet motor as a reason to relax chain safety.
Keep the chain sharp and tensioned, check bar oil each battery swap, and clean the motor vents. Batteries and charger are sold separately. See more battery-powered equipment.

faq.q: Does the T542iXP come with a battery?
faq.a: No. This is the bare tool. Batteries and charger are sold separately.

faq.q: Who should use a top-handle chainsaw?
faq.a: Trained arborists working in trees or aerial lifts. It is not a general ground saw.

name: Silky Zubat Replacement Blade, Fine Tooth
title: Silky Zubat Replacement Blade, Fine Tooth
h1: Silky Zubat Replacement Blade, Fine Tooth
meta: Silky Zubat replacement blade in fine tooth for cleaner pruning cuts on smaller limbs. How it differs from the standard blade, fitting tips and care.
tagline: A fine-tooth blade for the Silky Zubat handle, for smoother pruning cuts.
summary: The Silky Zubat replacement blade in fine tooth fits the Zubat handle and scabbard and gives a smoother cut than the standard tooth. It suits climbers who do a lot of detail pruning on smaller limbs.
highlights: Curved blade that pulls into the cut
Replaces a dull or damaged blade quickly
Cheaper than a whole new saw

p: The standard Zubat tooth cuts fast through mid-size limbs. The fine tooth trades a little speed for a smoother finish and less tearing, which helps on pruning cuts to a branch collar, small live wood and ornamental trees where a clean cut matters.

Silky's impulse-hardened teeth stay sharp a long time, but they are not made to be filed. When the blade dulls, bends or loses teeth, a new blade brings the saw back to new for much less than a complete saw.
Match the blade length to your Zubat handle and scabbard. The blade swaps with a screw at the handle; seat it fully and tighten before use. Wear gloves while handling the bare blade.
Wipe sap off with a little solvent or oil, and keep the saw in its scabbard. Never twist the blade in the cut or use it to pry. Find more replacement blades.

faq.q: Will a fine-tooth blade fit my Zubat handle?
faq.a: Yes, if the blade length matches your handle and scabbard.

faq.q: Can I sharpen a Silky blade?
faq.a: The teeth are hardened and not designed for filing. Replace the blade when it dulls.

name: Husqvarna 560BTS Backpack Blower
title: Husqvarna 560BTS Backpack Blower: 65cc Pro Blower
meta: Husqvarna 560BTS 65cc backpack blower for fast cleanup after tree work. Engine, harness, where it fits on a crew, plus fuel and maintenance tips.
tagline: A 65cc pro backpack blower for clearing sawdust, leaves and chips after tree work.
summary: The Husqvarna 560BTS is a 65cc gas backpack blower built for commercial crews. It moves sawdust, leaves and chipper debris quickly, so cleanup at the end of a tree job takes less time.
highlights: Backpack harness for long cleanup runs
Throttle on the tube for one-hand control

body.h: Cleanup is part of the job
p: Customers judge a tree job by how the yard looks when you leave. A strong backpack blower clears sawdust off driveways, blows chips out of beds and moves leaves into a pile for the chipper. The 560BTS has the output to do that fast on big properties.
The backpack layout puts the weight on your back rather than your arm, and the padded harness helps on long runs. The throttle on the tube lets you feather the air around flower beds and parked cars.

Run fresh mixed fuel at the ratio Husqvarna specifies, or use pre-mixed ethanol-free fuel for easier starts. Clean or replace the air filter regularly, check the spark plug, and keep the intake screen clear of leaves.
Wear hearing and eye protection, and keep the nozzle away from people and pets. Check local noise rules for early starts. See more blowers and equipment.

faq.q: What engine size is the Husqvarna 560BTS?
faq.a: It has a 65.6 cc two-stroke X-Torq engine.

faq.q: What fuel does it take?
faq.a: Mixed two-stroke fuel at Husqvarna's specified ratio. Pre-mixed ethanol-free fuel works well.

name: Best Management Practices: Tree Support Systems (Cabling, Bracing, Guying and Propping)
keyword: tree support systems best management practices
title: BMP: Tree Support Systems, Cabling and Bracing
h1: Best Management Practices: Tree Support Systems
meta: The ISA Best Management Practices guide to tree support systems covers cabling, bracing, guying and propping trees. Who it is for and what it covers.
tagline: ISA's practical guide to cabling, bracing, guying and propping trees.
summary: The ISA Best Management Practices guide to tree support systems explains how to plan, install and inspect cabling, bracing, guying and propping. It interprets the ANSI A300 support standard for working arborists.
highlights: Covers cabling, bracing, guying and propping
Interprets the ANSI A300 support standard
Explains when support is and is not appropriate

p: Cabling and bracing can extend the safe life of a tree, but only when the system is chosen and installed correctly. This BMP walks through assessing whether a tree is a good candidate, choosing between dynamic and static cables, setting through-rods for bracing, and when guying or propping is the better answer.
It is written to help arborists apply the ANSI A300 standard for support systems, with practical guidance on hardware placement, installation height and follow-up inspection.

Climbers moving into plant health care and support work, crew leaders who write work orders, and anyone studying for ISA certification will get the most out of it. It is also a useful reference to show customers why a system is installed a certain way.
A book is not a substitute for hands-on training. Learn installation under an experienced arborist. Browse more books and training materials.

faq.q: Who publishes the tree support systems BMP?
faq.a: The International Society of Arboriculture (ISA).

faq.q: Does it replace ANSI A300?
faq.a: No. It is a companion that helps you apply the standard in the field.

name: Best Practices for SRT in Arboriculture
title: Best Practices for SRT in Arboriculture
h1: Best Practices for SRT in Arboriculture
meta: Best Practices for SRT in Arboriculture is a training guide to single rope technique for tree climbers: systems, anchors, devices and safe working habits.
tagline: A training reference on single rope technique for working arborists.
summary: Best Practices for SRT in Arboriculture is a training reference on single rope technique (SRT) for tree climbers. It helps climbers moving from doubled-rope systems understand anchors, devices and safe habits for working on a stationary rope.
highlights: Focused on single rope technique for tree work
Covers anchors, ascent and work positioning
Good for climbers moving from MRS to SRS

p: Single rope technique has changed how many arborists climb. Ascending a fixed line is faster and less tiring than body-thrusting on a doubled rope, and a stationary rope system can be set from the ground with a throw line. It also brings new risks: anchor forces, base-tie choices and device selection all matter more.
A focused guide helps climbers understand the reasoning behind SRS setups, not just the steps, so they can make good choices in trees that do not match the textbook.

Use the book alongside hands-on training with a qualified climber. Practice every system low and slow before working at height, follow ANSI Z133 and device makers' instructions, and inspect your gear before each climb.
It makes a good reference for crew training sessions and for climbers preparing for certification. Browse more books and training materials.

faq.q: Is this book for beginners?
faq.a: It suits climbers with some experience who are learning or refining SRT. Beginners should start with hands-on training.

faq.q: Can I learn SRT from a book alone?
faq.a: No. Use it with in-person training from a qualified climber.

name: Groundie Training Book
title: Groundie: Training Book for Tree Care Ground Workers
meta: Groundie is a training book for tree care ground workers: rigging support, chipper safety, drop zones and communication with the climber. Who it is for.
tagline: A training book for the ground worker on a tree care crew.
summary: Groundie is a training book for the ground worker on a tree care crew, the person who runs the lowering line, feeds the chipper and keeps the drop zone safe. It covers the skills that make a good groundie and a safer job site.
highlights: Written for tree care ground workers

body.h: Why ground work deserves its own book
p: The groundie runs the friction on the lowering line, watches the drop zone, sends gear up, hauls brush and feeds the chipper. Much of the crew's safety depends on that person, yet ground workers often learn on the job by trial and error.

A training book gives new hires the basics in one place: knots and rigging support, clear communication with the climber, chipper safety, and keeping the work zone controlled around customers and traffic.

Hand it to new ground workers in their first weeks and go over chapters during tailgate safety meetings. Pair reading with hands-on practice, and follow ANSI Z133 and your company's procedures on every job.
Experienced climbers can use it to explain what they expect from the ground. Browse more books and training materials.

faq.q: Who should read Groundie?
faq.a: New tree care ground workers, and crew leaders who train them.

faq.q: Does it replace job-site training?
faq.a: No. Use it alongside supervised hands-on training.

name: The Tree Climber's Companion
title: The Tree Climber's Companion by Jeff Jepson
meta: The Tree Climber's Companion by Jeff Jepson: a pocket guide to tree climbing knots, systems and techniques for arborists. Who it suits and how to use it.
tagline: Jeff Jepson's pocket-size field guide to tree climbing knots and techniques.
summary: The Tree Climber's Companion by Jeff Jepson is a compact, illustrated guide to the knots, gear and techniques of tree climbing. It is a long-standing favorite for new climbers and a handy refresher for experienced ones.
highlights: Written by arborist trainer Jeff Jepson
Compact size for the truck or gear bag
Covers gear, tie-ins and work positioning
Good study aid for new climbers

p: The book covers the essentials of climbing a tree for work: rope and hardware, the knots and hitches used in climbing and rigging, ascent methods, tie-in points, and positioning in the crown. Clear illustrations make knots easy to follow, and the small size means it can live in a gear bag.
Because it covers fundamentals, it suits new climbers learning a doubled-rope system and experienced climbers who want to check a knot they rarely tie.

Practice each knot and system on the ground before you use it at height, and learn under a qualified climber. Gear and techniques evolve, so pair the book with current manufacturer instructions and ANSI Z133.
Many crews keep a copy in the truck for training days. Pair it with Jepson's other titles, and browse more books and training materials.

faq.q: Who wrote The Tree Climber's Companion?
faq.a: Jeff Jepson, an arborist and climbing instructor.

faq.q: Is it good for beginners?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the most common first books for new tree climbers.

name: To Fell a Tree
title: To Fell a Tree by Jeff Jepson: Felling Guide
meta: To Fell a Tree by Jeff Jepson is a practical, illustrated guide to tree felling: notches, hinges, back cuts, wedges and planning a safe escape route.
tagline: Jeff Jepson's illustrated guide to planning and making safe felling cuts.
summary: To Fell a Tree by Jeff Jepson is an illustrated guide to tree felling, from sizing up the tree to the notch, hinge and back cut. It is written for arborists, loggers and landowners who want to fell with more control.
highlights: Written by arborist trainer Jeff Jepson
Illustrated notch, hinge and back cut methods
Covers wedges, pulling lines and escape routes
Fits in the truck for reference

p: Felling goes right when the planning is right. The book walks through assessing lean, defects and hazards, choosing a lay, clearing escape routes and then making the cuts: open-face and conventional notches, hinge sizing, bore cuts and back cuts. It also covers wedges and pull lines for trees that need help.
Clear drawings show what a good hinge looks like and what goes wrong when it is cut through or left too thick.
A book cannot replace hands-on chainsaw and felling training. Learn under a qualified instructor, wear full saw PPE including chaps, helmet, eye and hearing protection, and follow ANSI Z133.
Use it to prepare for training, to review before a tricky removal and to teach new crew members the reasoning behind each cut. Browse more books and training materials.

faq.q: Who wrote To Fell a Tree?
faq.a: Jeff Jepson, also author of The Tree Climber's Companion.

faq.q: Is To Fell a Tree for beginners?
faq.a: Yes, it explains fundamentals clearly, but it should be used with hands-on training.

name: Fiberglass Scuff Pad with Step
title: Fiberglass Bucket Scuff Pad with Step
meta: Fiberglass scuff pad with step for aerial lift buckets: protects the bucket from wear and gives a step up for getting in and out. Fit and safety notes.
tagline: A fiberglass bucket protector with a built-in step for aerial lift work.
summary: A fiberglass scuff pad with step fits over the edge of an aerial lift bucket to protect it from wear and gives the operator a step for getting in and out. It is a simple upgrade for tree and utility bucket trucks.
highlights: Protects the bucket lip and wall from wear
Built-in step for easier entry and exit

p: Bucket walls take a beating from boots, saws, branches and the boom rest. A scuff pad takes that wear instead of the bucket, and the built-in step makes climbing in and out at ground level easier and steadier, especially in wet or muddy conditions.
Swapping a worn pad is much cheaper than repairing or replacing a damaged bucket.
Measure your bucket and check the pad's fit before ordering. Install it per the instructions and make sure it does not interfere with the bucket's liner, controls or tool holders.

Fiberglass does not make an unrated bucket insulated. Follow the lift maker's instructions, OSHA and ANSI Z133 for electrical clearances, and wear your fall arrest harness and lanyard whenever you are in the bucket. Inspect the pad for cracks and loose mounts. See more bucket truck accessories.

faq.q: What does a bucket scuff pad do?
faq.a: It protects the bucket from wear and gives you a step for getting in and out.

faq.q: Does a fiberglass pad affect bucket insulation?
faq.a: It does not add insulation rating. Follow your lift's dielectric rating and required clearances.
